                    ### Question
                    A 25-year old Caucasian female presents with symptoms of Graves' disease. Her doctor prescribes medications and sends the patient home. After two months of therapy, the patient returns upset that her exophthalmos has not gone away. Which of the following drugs should the physician have prescribed to treat the exophthalmos?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
To treat exophthalmos in Graves' disease, the physician should have prescribed corticosteroids. Corticosteroids have anti-inflammatory properties that can help reduce the inflammation and swelling behind the eyes, which are the underlying causes of exophthalmos in Graves' disease. PTU may indirectly improve exophthalmos by controlling thyroid hormone levels, but corticosteroids directly target the inflammation. Propanolol and Metoprolol, although beta-blockers used to manage other symptoms of Graves' disease, do not directly treat exophthalmos. No treatment relying on natural resolution may not be effective in all cases.
